title: Kisslinger Glassworks Rattenberg
name: Kisslinger Glassworks Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Schauglashütte Kisslinger in Rattenberg: rich glassmaking tradition across 1,000 m², glowing furnaces, glassblowing demonstrations, and engraving.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Schauglashütte Kisslinger is situated in the heart of the medieval town of Rattenberg – Austria's smallest town – in the Tyrolean Unterinntal at an altitude of 521 metres. Rattenberg enjoys worldwide acclaim as a storied "glass town" whose artisan craftsmanship dates back to the 19th century. In the headquarters of the Kisslinger family, visitors explore over 1,000 square metres of exhibition and workshop space, experiencing the centuries-old fascination of glassblowing and glass engraving right beside glowing melting furnaces.

Glassmaking Craft & Demonstration Workshop

For multiple generations, the Kisslinger family business has combined traditional glass refining techniques with contemporary design. The core of the visitor experience is the open Schauwerkstatt: at temperatures exceeding 1,200 °C, glassmakers gather viscous molten glass from the furnaces using blowpipes, blow it into wooden moulds, and shape exquisite vases, bowls, and delicate glasses with skilled hand movements. Visitors can watch the master craftsmen directly over their shoulders to see how unique works of art emerge from red-hot glass. In adjacent demonstration studios, engravers, glass cutters, and glass painters showcase exquisite finishing techniques featuring diamond-point engraving, coat-of-arms etching, and vibrant colours. The spacious showrooms display fine lead crystal, sparkling glass jewellery, modern home accessories, and traditional Tyrolean schnapps glasses.

Visit & Getting There

The Schauglashütte Kisslinger is open year-round from Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 18:00 (Sundays from May to October from 10:00 to 17:00; glassblowing demonstrations Monday to Friday during working hours). Admission to the demonstration workshop and exhibition rooms is free! By prior arrangement, visitors can even blow their own glass sphere under expert guidance. By train: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Rattenberg-Kramsach station, from where it is just a two-minute walk through the historic town gate into the pedestrian zone at Südtiroler Straße 40. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kramsach, and park in the large car parks P1 to P3 on the outskirts of Rattenberg (Rattenberg is a pedestrian-only zone).

Tips

The exhibition rooms and the demonstration workshop on the ground floor are step-free and barrier-free for wheelchair users and strollers. Treat yourself to fresh Tyrolean apple strudel in one of Rattenberg's traditional pastry shops before strolling through the picturesque alleys of the glass town.
